children: BSE shares fell 3 percent on Friday, snapping gains in the previous session, after the National Stock Exchange (NSE) announced the price band for its upcoming initial public offering (IPO).

The BSE stock has declined in three of the last four sessions and is now hovering near a key support zone, according to analysts. A decisive breach of this level could trigger fresh selling pressure, they added.

The NSE IPO will open for subscription on September 17 and close on September 21. Bidding by anchor investors will take place on September 16. The price band has been fixed at Rs 1,700-1,785 per share.
Sudeep Shah, Head of Technical and Derivatives Research at SBI Securities, said BSE has been consolidating in the 3,474-3,132 range since August 17.
"The falling ADX indicates a lack of trend strength, while the MACD line remains below the zero line, pointing to weak momentum," Shah said.

He said the immediate support for the stock is in the 3,130-3,100 zone. "Any decisive breakdown below this zone could invite fresh selling pressure and drag the stock lower towards the next support at 2,970," he said.
On the upside, the 3,350-3,370 zone is likely to act as an immediate resistance, Shah said.
Earlier, Bernstein had initiated coverage on BSE with an 'underperform' rating.

The cautious view comes amid broader concerns over trading volumes at BSE. The exchange's management has acknowledged that the recently introduced Closing Auction Session (CAS) has resulted in lower index options volumes, with limited liquidity in the auction session affecting participation.
Bernstein, meanwhile, has taken a more constructive view of Multi Commodity Exchange of India (MCX), initiating coverage with an 'outperform' rating.
BSE currently commands a market capitalisation of more than Rs 1.31 lakh crore.

With the NSE IPO, investors are also comparing the valuations and profitability of the two exchanges. NSE has a market capitalisation of around Rs 4.46 lakh crore, FY26 profit after tax (PAT) of Rs 10,302 crore and a price-to-earnings (P/E) multiple of about 42.5 times.
BSE, by comparison, has a market capitalisation of around Rs 1.31 lakh crore, FY26 PAT of Rs 2,497 crore and a P/E multiple of about 49 times.
At the NSE IPO valuation, the exchange would be worth about 3.2 times BSE while generating more than four times the profit.
